identity.title: [v0.92][WP-02B][build] Run the post-migration build acceleration experiment

values.task_boundary: Deliver a measured and reversible post-migration build acceleration decision for the standard and 16-core GitHub-hosted runner comparison.
deliverables: Migration-eligibility receipt and frozen workload/environment manifest
Raw five-cold and ten-warm trial records for each platform and selected workload
Queue, cache, timing, reliability, proof-parity, and cost analysis
Restricted runner-group access, concurrency, budget, and rollback evidence
One production-semantics canary and lane-by-lane adopt/reject/defer decision
Ten-run post-change observation for adopted routes or cleanup confirmation for rejected routes
acceptance_criteria: WP-02 migration and WP-02A CI reliability gates are verified before paid execution
Control and candidate runs use one exact commit, workflow, toolchain, lockfiles, commands, permissions, cache design, and proof input set
Five cold and ten warm trials per selected workload and platform retain cache classification, queue delay, failures, retries, cancellations, and justified outliers
Result, artifact, validation, and required-check semantics are equivalent before the canary
The decision table reports p50, p95, critical-path delta, queue delta, cost, reliability, and proof parity against predeclared thresholds
No route is adopted without threshold compliance and a successful canary; adopted routes retain fallback and ten-run observation evidence
Rejected or deferred routing is removed without product-code or test-expectation changes
Failure, security, privacy, portability, recovery, cost, and claim boundaries are tested or explicitly dispositioned
One exact-revision pre-PR review has no unresolved actionable findings
dependencies: Agent Logic organization-owner approval for budget and selected-repository runner access
non_goals: AWS or a self-hosted runner platform
Changes to validation breadth, test semantics, required-check names, or branch protection
32-core, coverage-topology, custom-image, ARM64, or self-hosted experiments
Treating runner provisioning, cache existence, or planning prose as acceleration proof
